title: Formalization, Transparency, and Collusion in Open-Source Game Theory
abstract: arXiv:2611.33193v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Cooperation among AI agents will undermine alignment protocols when it takes the form of collusion. Under these protocols, agents often have some information about one another, and how much they have may determine whether they collude. Open-source game theory studies the extreme case, in which each program reads its opponent's source code and acts based on what it can prove about it. We develop formal foundations for this theory: we specify a concrete proof system, resolve an open problem concerning DupocBot and CupodBot through a transposition argument, and mechanize the framework in Lean 4; to our knowledge, this is the first mechanization of resource-bounded open-source game theory. We then extend the framework to the more realistic setting of partial transparency, where each program receives only partial information about its opponent. translated_title: 开源博弈论中的形式化、透明性与共谋
translated_abstract: AI智能体之间的合作一旦表现为共谋形式，就会破坏对齐协议。在这些协议下，智能体通常对彼此拥有一定的信息，而信息量的多少可能决定它们是否共谋。开源博弈论研究了极端情形：每个程序读取对手的源代码，并根据它能够证明的内容来采取行动。我们为这一理论建立了形式化基础：我们规定了一个具体的证明系统，通过转置论证解决了关于DupocBot和CupodBot的开放问题，并在Lean 4中对该框架进行了机械化验证；据我们所知，这是首次对资源受限开源博弈论进行机械化。随后，我们将该框架扩展到更现实的部分透明性设定，即每个程序只能获得关于对手的部分信息。在囚徒困境实验中（其中相互合作模拟共谋），更大的透明性……
tldr: 该论文为开源博弈论建立了形式化基础，首次在Lean 4中机械化验证了资源受限的开源博弈论框架，并通过囚徒困境实验探究了部分透明性如何影响AI智能体之间的共谋行为。
en_tdlr: This paper establishes formal foundations for open-source game theory, provides the first Lean 4 mechanization of resource-bounded open-source game theory, and investigates how partial transparency influences collusion among AI agents through Prisoner's Dilemma experiments.
